title: Most Profit Assigning Work
summary: Given n jobs and m workers, with arrays for job difficulty, profit, and worker abilities, determine the maximum profit by assigning each worker to at most one job they can complete.
statement: Given n jobs and m workers, with arrays for job difficulty, profit, and worker abilities, determine the maximum profit by assigning each worker to at most one job they can complete. If a worker cannot complete any job, their profit is $0.
constraints: Jobs may be reused by multiple workers; each worker chooses one job at or below ability.
hints: As worker ability increases, the set of feasible jobs only grows.
Sort jobs and workers; sweep once while maintaining best feasible profit.
Advance jobs with difficulty<=skill, update best, and add best for each worker.
The running maximum summarizes every feasible job, and job reuse makes worker choices independent.
editorial: The running maximum summarizes every feasible job, and job reuse makes worker choices independent.

tests.explanation: No worker can perform any listed job, so profit is zero.
